value.rationale: The canonical hypersimplex interpolates regular simplices and uniform-matroid base polytopes, so its minimum intrinsic Euclidean width and the complete optimal-support orientation set are natural geometric invariants. The exact difference body and the two norm barriers explain a real structural change between coordinate and balanced sign directions. A complete phase equation with genuinely different tied normal orbits at n=4m²−1, first at n=15,k=2, is a meaningful all-dimensional classification rather than an arbitrary slice or a textbook restatement of the previously known simplex case.
